title: On the sum-of-digits measures and Cusick's conjecture via stopped random walks
summary: Let $s(n)$ denote the number of ones in the binary expansion of a natural number $n\in\mathbb{N}$. For any $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and $d\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $μ_t(d)$ denote the asymptotic density of the set of those natural numbers $n$ for which $s(n+t)-s(n)=d$. The $μ_t$ are properly defined probability measures on $\Z$, and the Cusick conjecture states that $μ_t(\mathbb{N})>\frac{1}{2}$ for any $t\in\mathbb{N}$.
